extracted.intended_audience: book reviewers, book bloggers, and reviewers considering joining Reedsy Discovery (ARC platforms)
extracted.subtask_description: A blogger’s practical evaluation checklist for joining or using an ARC/review marketplace (specifically Reedsy Discovery) from a reviewer’s perspective. Focuses on usability, reviewer onboarding, monetization, selection, author costs, and reviewer safety/ethics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer verification / application process
rubrics_metrics.description: You must apply to be a reviewer; acceptance appears to depend on having a social media/Goodreads presence and can be completed in a matter of days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider how hard it is to become a verified reviewer and what profile merits acceptance; the author guessed social media/Goodreads presence matters. Verification gate can limit the reviewer pool and affects access to books.

rubrics_metrics.name: Website usability / navigation / UI quality
rubrics_metrics.description: The website is easy to navigate and visually appealing — described as 'the slickest UI' the author has seen on any ARC site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ease of finding books and clarity of site features matters to reviewers. A slick UI reduces friction for discovering and accepting review opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer monetization options (tips & referrals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reedsy Discovery allows readers to tip reviewers and gives reviewers referral codes that pay $50 if someone signs up and leaves a review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monetization options (tips, referral payouts) are a reviewer benefit other ARC sites may not offer; evaluate frequency of payouts and likelihood of earning tips or referral rewards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trustworthiness of payouts / marketplace payments
rubrics_metrics.description: Reedsy's wider marketplace shows verified posts of people being paid for services (e.g., ghostwriting), suggesting they do pay out referral/marketplace earnings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence of other payouts on Reedsy’s marketplace is a positive signal, but reviewers should verify actual referral/refund/payment policies before relying on them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author pricing model and cost-to-author
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors pay $50 for the chance of getting one review — the platform charges per review-opportunity rather than guaranteeing widespread coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should be aware authors have paid for a chance at review; this raises questions about value for money and fairness. Authors’ cost structure may affect the volume and quality of submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of reviews / fulfillment and refund policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may pay and still not receive a review; at least one author was able to get a refund after not getting a review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the platform’s track record for delivering promised reviews and its refund policies. This affects both author trust and reviewer expectations about uptake of listings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer anonymity / risk of being identified by authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Because there may be few reviewers on a given book (sometimes only one), a negative review could make it easy for the author to identify and track down the reviewer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the platform’s reviewer exposure: being the only reviewer for a paid submission risks conflict or harassment. Platforms where reviewers are one among many provide more buffer for candid reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Size and genre breadth of book selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Book selection may be small in some genres (example: only 19 books tagged as romance, zero cozy mysteries at time of writing), and results sometimes include books whose main tag is not the searched genre.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the catalog includes sufficient titles in your preferred genres and whether genre tagging/search is accurate; a limited or poorly tagged catalog reduces useful options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy of genre tagging / search results
rubrics_metrics.description: Searches returned books that were not actually in the searched genre (e.g., listed romance results whose main tag was women’s fiction or urban fantasy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poor tagging/search results increase time spent filtering and may frustrate reviewers seeking specific genres. Test search reliability before committing to regular reviewing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency of the review-request & communication process
rubrics_metrics.description: The author could not test the process of getting a book or communicating with authors and therefore could not comment on these aspects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Platforms should make the steps for accepting books, receiving files, and communicating expectations with authors clear; lack of transparency is a drawback and reviewers should seek sample workflows or FAQs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical perception of paid-for review model
rubrics_metrics.description: There is tension about authors paying for reviews: some find it suspicious that authors pay for reviews (author initially skeptical), while others argue $50 for a vetted editorial review is a bargain compared to paid editorial services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider how paid submission models affect perceived impartiality and reviewer integrity. Reviewers should weigh reputation risks and decide whether the platform’s vetting and reviewer independence policies mitigate concerns.
